meta.title: The Banana Seller
meta.textType: story: an interview with a banana seller

paragraphs: At ten o'clock on Saturday, January twenty-third, the Explorers walked through the market in pairs. First, they passed a stall of mangoes. Then they passed a stall with noisy ducks in a cage. Next, they came to a stall of fried bananas. May and Lily went to look at a stall of peppers. Leo and Mia stopped at the banana stall. The seller was a man in a gray apron. He fried bananas in a big, heavy pan. The sign said "FRIED BANANAS," and one piece cost ten baht. The man held up a piece on a stick and smiled.

"Would you tell us about your stall?" asked Leo. "Of course," said the seller. "How long have you sold bananas?" asked Leo. "For twenty years," said the seller. Mia wrote in her notebook. "Would you say that again, please?" she asked. "I sell forty bananas a day," said the seller. Leo made a joke. "I am not a monkey, but I love bananas," he said. The seller laughed and said, "I am a big fan of jokes." Then he offered each child a hot piece in a small paper bag. Leo held his bag and said thank you.

At noon, the pairs met Teacher Kim at the fruit stall by the pier. Teacher Kim bought a paper cup of fruit for each child. The boats were on the river behind them. The children ate and read their notebooks. "What did you learn?" asked Teacher Kim. "The banana seller is a friendly guy," said Mia. She read her notes. "He has sold bananas for twenty years, and he sells forty bananas a day." "A banana is a snack, but forty bananas are a lot of work," said Leo.

Then May read her notes. "The woman at the pepper stall has a variety of peppers," she said. "They are red, green, and yellow." "She is meeting her sister at one o'clock, so she is closing early." "Many stalls sell snacks," said Lily. "A few of them sell a full meal." Teacher Kim laughed. "Every stall has a seller, and every seller has a story," she said.

"On Monday, Lily and May are writing the blog post," said Teacher Kim. "Leo is drawing a cartoon of the banana seller, and Mia is choosing the photos." Leo looked at his empty paper bag and smiled. "I am sure that we have a good story," he said.
text.summary: At the market, Leo and Mia interview a man who fries bananas. He has sold bananas for twenty years, laughs at Leo's joke, and offers each child a piece, and later the pairs share their notes with Teacher Kim.
